# fs_extra - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fs_extra/

Copies a list of directories and files to another place recursively. This function will
also copy the permission bits of the original files to destination files (not for
directories).

Copies a list of directories and files to another place recursively, with
information about progress. This function will also copy the permission bits of the
original files to destination files (not for directories).

Moves a list of directories and files to another place recursively. This function will
also copy the permission bits of the original files to destination files (not for
directories).

Moves a list of directories and files to another place recursively, with
information about progress. This function will also copy the permission bits of the
original files to destination files (not for directories).

# fs_extra 1.3.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fs_extra/latest

# fs_extra

A Rust library that provides additional functionality not present in [ std::fs](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/index.html).

## Key features:

-
Copy files (optionally with information about the progress).
-
Copy directories recursively (optionally with information about the progress).
-
Move files (optionally with information about the progress).
-
Move directories recursively (optionally with information about the progress).
-
A single method for create and write `String`content in file.
-
A single method for open and read `String`content from file.
-
Get folder size
-
Get collection of directory entries

## Functions:

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| [fs_extra::copy_items](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/fn.copy_items.html) | Recursively copies files and directories from one location to another |
| [fs_extra::copy_items_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/fn.copy_items_with_progress.html) | Recursively copies files and directories from one location to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::move_items](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/fn.move_items.html) | Recursively moves files and directories from one location to another |
| [fs_extra::move_items_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/fn.move_items_with_progress.html) | Recursively moves files and directories from one location to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::remove_items](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/fn.remove_items.html) | Removes files or directories |
| [fs_extra::file::copy](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.copy.html) | Copies the contents of one file to another |
| [fs_extra::file::copy_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.copy_with_progress.html) | Copies the contents of one file to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::file::move_file](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.move_file.html) | Moves a file from one location to another |
| [fs_extra::file::move_file_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.move_file_with_progress.html) | Moves a file from one location to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::file::remove](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.remove.html) | Removes a file |
| [fs_extra::file::read_to_string](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.read_to_string.html) | Reads file content into a `String` |
| [fs_extra::file::write_all](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.write_all.html) | Writes `String`content to a file |
| [fs_extra::dir::create](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.create.html) | Creates a new, empty directory at the given path |
| [fs_extra::dir::create_all](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.create_all.html) | Recursively creates a directory and all of its parent components if they are missing |
| [fs_extra::dir::copy](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.copy.html) | Recursively copies the directory contents from one location to another |
| [fs_extra::dir::copy_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.copy_with_progress.html) | Recursively copies the directory contents from one location to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::dir::move_dir](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.move_dir.html) | Moves directory contents from one location to another |
| [fs_extra::dir::move_dir_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.move_dir_with_progress.html) | Moves directory contents from one location to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::dir::remove](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.remove.html) | Removes directory |
| [fs_extra::dir::get_size](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.get_size.html) | Returns the size of the file or directory |
| [fs_extra::dir::get_dir_content](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.get_dir_content.html) | Gets details such as the size and child items of a directory |
| [fs_extra::dir::get_dir_content2](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.get_dir_content2.html) | Gets details such as the size and child items of a directory using specified settings |
| [fs_extra::dir::get_details_entry](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.get_details_entry.html) | Gets attributes of a directory entry |
| [fs_extra::dir::ls](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.ls.html) | Gets attributes of directory entries in a directory |

## Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "1.3.0"
```
## Examples

The following example shows how to copy a directory recursively and display progress. First a source directory `./temp/dir` containing file `test1.txt` and a subdirectory `sub` is createad with `sub` itself having a file `test2.txt`. `./temp/dir` and all contents are then copied out to `./out/dir`.

```
use Path;
use ;
use ;
extern crate fs_extra;
use *;
use *;
```

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# surtgis_algorithms - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-algorithms/0.17.0/surtgis_algorithms/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#surtgis-algorithms)SurtGis Algorithms

Geospatial analysis algorithms for SurtGis.

[§](https://docs.rs#available-algorithm-categories)Available Algorithm Categories

- **terrain**: Slope, aspect, hillshade, curvature, TPI, TRI, landform, TWI, SPI, STI, geomorphons, viewshed, SVF, openness, convergence, multiscale curvatures, feature-preserving smoothing, wind exposure, solar radiation, MRVBF/MRRTF, northness/eastness, DEV, multidirectional hillshade, shape index, curvedness, log transform, accumulation zones
- **hydrology**: Fill sinks, Priority-Flood, flow direction, flow accumulation, watershed, HAND, stream network
- **imagery**: Spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, NDRE, GNDVI, NGRDI, RECI, etc.), band math, reclassification
- **interpolation**: IDW, nearest neighbor, TIN
- **vector**: Buffer, simplify, spatial operations, clipping, measurements
- **morphology**: Erosion, dilation, opening, closing, gradient, top-hat, black-hat
- **statistics**: Focal statistics, zonal statistics, spatial autocorrelation

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [classification](https://docs.rs/classification/index.html)
- Classification and machine learning algorithms for raster data
- [fluvial](https://docs.rs/fluvial/index.html)
- Fluvial-tectonic morphometry.
- [hydrology](https://docs.rs/hydrology/index.html)
- Hydrological analysis algorithms
- [imagery](https://docs.rs/imagery/index.html)
- Imagery analysis algorithms

- Spatial interpolation algorithms
- [landscape](https://docs.rs/landscape/index.html)
- Landscape ecology algorithms
- [morphology](https://docs.rs/morphology/index.html)
- Mathematical morphology algorithms for raster processing
- [pansharpening](https://docs.rs/pansharpening/index.html)
- Pansharpening: fuse a high-resolution panchromatic image with a lower-resolution multispectral image to produce a high-resolution multispectral output.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Prelude for convenient imports
- [sampling](https://docs.rs/sampling/index.html)
- Raster sampling primitives: point extraction, CNN patches, and polygon grid sampling.
- [segmentation](https://docs.rs/segmentation/index.html)
- Image segmentation algorithms.
- [statistics](https://docs.rs/statistics/index.html)
- Statistical analysis algorithms for raster data

- Terrain analysis algorithms
- [texture](https://docs.rs/texture/index.html)
- Texture and feature extraction algorithms
- [vector](https://docs.rs/vector/index.html)
- Vector analysis algorithms

# tatara_net - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tatara-net/0.2.122/tatara_net/

## Expand description

tatara-net: Cross-platform networking plane for the tatara cluster fabric.

The complete sandwich:

```
┌─ WASI (wasmtime) ──── Portable, sandboxed workloads ─────────┐
├─ Tatara Runtime ───── Convergence, scheduling, Raft ─────────┤
├─ eBPF (aya) ────────── Kernel hooks, pure Rust ──────────────┤
├─ WireGuard (mamorigami) ─ Encrypted mesh fabric ─────────────┤
└─ Hardware ──────────── Abstracted away ──────────────────────┘
```
On Linux: eBPF programs (XDP/TC/cgroup) for kernel-level networking. On macOS: userspace networking via tun-rs + smoltcp + hanabi proxy. Everywhere: WireGuard mesh via mamorigami for encrypted inter-node traffic.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use config::`- [NetConfig](https://docs.rs/config/struct.NetConfig.html);
- `pub use traits::`- [NetworkPlane](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.NetworkPlane.html);
- `pub use`- [types](https://docs.rs/types/index.html)::*;

- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- Networking plane configuration.
- [convergence](https://docs.rs/convergence/index.html)
- Module stub — implementation in later phases.
- [mesh](https://docs.rs/mesh/index.html)
- Module stub — implementation in later phases.
- [observability](https://docs.rs/observability/index.html)
- Module stub — implementation in later phases.

# tatara_wasm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tatara-wasm/0.2.122/tatara_wasm/

## Expand description

`tatara-wasm` — multi-runtime WASI/WASM host for tatara guests.

Five runtimes, one trait, Cargo feature flags. Consumers pick the runtime per workload via the Lisp surface:

```
(defguest fast-fn   :kind (:wasm :runtime :wasmtime …))
(defguest k8s-fn    :kind (:wasm :runtime :wasmedge …))
(defguest embed-fn  :kind (:wasm :runtime :wamr   :features (:aot #t :no-std #t)))
```
The runtime axis is first-class — all five are shipped with
production-grade implementations in Phase H.3 (wasmtime) and
H.4 (the rest). See `docs/declarative-guests.md`.

[§](https://docs.rs#status)Status

**Phase H.1 stub.** The `WasmRuntime` enum + `WasmEngine` trait
land here now so `tatara-vm` can reference them. Runtime bodies
are empty until H.3/H.4.

# surtgis_colormap - Rust

Color mapping and raster-to-RGBA rendering for SurtGis.

# sequoia_openpgp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sequoia-openpgp/2.4.0/sequoia_openpgp/

## Expand description

OpenPGP data types and associated machinery.

This crate aims to provide a complete implementation of OpenPGP as
defined by [RFC 9580](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9580.html) as well as the deprecated OpenPGP as defined
by [RFC 4880](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4880).  OpenPGP is a standard by the IETF.  It was derived
from the PGP software, which was created by Phil Zimmermann in
1991.

This crate also includes support for unbuffered message processing.

A few features that the OpenPGP community considers to be deprecated (e.g., version 3 compatibility) have been left out. We have also updated some OpenPGP defaults to avoid foot guns (e.g., we selected modern algorithm defaults). If some functionality is missing, please file a bug report.

A non-goal of this crate is support for any sort of high-level,
bolted-on functionality.  For instance, [RFC 9580](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9580.html) does not define
trust models, such as the web of trust, direct trust, or TOFU.
Neither does this crate.  [RFC 9580](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9580.html) does provide some mechanisms
for creating trust models (specifically, UserID certifications),
and this crate does expose those mechanisms.

We also try hard to avoid dictating how OpenPGP should be used. This doesn’t mean that we don’t have opinions about how OpenPGP should be used in a number of common scenarios (for instance, message validation). But, in this crate, we refrain from expressing those opinions; we will expose an opinionated, high-level interface in the future. In order to figure out the most appropriate high-level interfaces, we look at existing users. If you are using Sequoia, please get in contact so that we can learn from your use cases, discuss your opinions, and develop a high-level interface based on these experiences in the future.

Despite —or maybe because of— its unopinionated nature we found it easy to develop opinionated OpenPGP software based on Sequoia.

[§](https://docs.rs#experimental-features)Experimental Features

This crate may implement extensions where the standardization effort is still ongoing. These experimental features are marked as such in the documentation. We invite you to experiment with them, but please do expect the semantics and possibly even the wire format to evolve.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [anyhow](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- ASCII Armor.
- [cert](https://docs.rs/cert/index.html)
- Certificates and related data structures.
- [crypto](https://docs.rs/crypto/index.html)
- Cryptographic primitives.
- [fmt](https://docs.rs/fmt/index.html)
- Utilities for formatting, printing, and user communication.
- [message](https://docs.rs/message/index.html)
- Message support.
- [packet](https://docs.rs/packet/index.html)
- Packet-related data types.

- Packet parsing infrastructure.

- A mechanism to specify policy.

- OpenPGP regex parser.

# tatara_hvf - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tatara-hvf/0.2.122/tatara_hvf/

## Expand description

`tatara-hvf` — Apple Hypervisor.framework backend for tatara guests.

The **bare-metal** VM engine. Direct `hv_vm_*` / `hv_vcpu_*` calls
via the `applevisor` safe-wrapper crate, own virtio device backends
(landing H.2.2), raw vCPU loop with MMIO callbacks.

[§](https://docs.rs#layering)Layering

```
  tatara-hvf (this crate)
      │  uses
      ▼
  applevisor (safe wrapper — Quarkslab)
      │  links
      ▼
  Hypervisor.framework  (aarch64-darwin only)
```
[§](https://docs.rs#cargo--build)Cargo / build

The `applevisor` dep is target-gated to `aarch64-darwin`. On any
other target, the crate compiles but `HvfEngine::new()` returns
`HvfError::UnsupportedPlatform`. This keeps `cargo check --workspace` clean on Linux CI while the real engine is only
exercised on M-series Macs.

[§](https://docs.rs#entitlements)Entitlements

Running any HVF binary requires the `com.apple.security.hypervisor`
entitlement. For `cargo test`, either codesign the test binary
with an entitlements plist or run tests as root. Currently:

```
codesign --entitlements entitlements.plist --sign - \
  target/debug/deps/tatara_hvf-*
```
A follow-up CI helper crate will encapsulate this; for now the
`vm_create_is_supported` test is `#[ignore]` by default so `cargo test` doesn’t fail when entitlements aren’t set.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use stub::`- [HvfEngine](https://docs.rs/stub/struct.HvfEngine.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [stub](https://docs.rs/stub/index.html)
- Non-aarch64-darwin stub. HVF doesn’t exist on Linux / Intel Mac, so
`HvfEngine::new()`returns a typed error. The struct still exists so downstream crates compile.

- A guest memory region mapped into the VM’s physical address space.

- Page permissions for a mapped region.

- Errors from the HVF backend.

# tatara_build_remote - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tatara-build-remote/0.2.122/tatara_build_remote/

## Expand description

`tatara-build-remote` — layered Nix build transport for tatara guests.

Takes a `BuildRef` (flake + attr, raw Nix expression, store path, or
OCI image) and resolves it to a concrete `StorePath` using a
priority-ordered chain of transports. **First match wins.** Default
chain:

- **Attic cache**— pulls from a shared Attic instance (e.g.- `quero.lol`). Fastest path when the artifact is already cached.
- **ssh-ng remote builder**— submits to a remote Nix builder over- `ssh-ng://`. Used when Attic misses and the local machine can’t or shouldn’t build (cross-arch, resource constrained, etc.).
- **Local**—- `nix build`on the host. Last resort.

Any transport declared absent in the spec is skipped. If all declared
transports fail, `BuildError::AllTransportsFailed` bubbles up and
hospedeiro refuses to boot the guest — we fail closed.

[§](https://docs.rs#status)Status

**Phase H.5 landed.** `AtticTransport`, `SshRemoteTransport`, and
`LocalTransport` all ship in `transports.rs`.
`BuildTransportChain::to_layered()` composes them into a priority-
ordered `LayeredTransport` driven by `(defguest …)`’s `:build-on`
keyword.

[§](https://docs.rs#why-layered-not-single-target)Why layered, not single-target

The fleet at `quero.lol` has a shared Attic cache *and* an ssh-ng
builder pool. Cache hits are free; builds are expensive. Layering
lets the common case (pleme-io team members pulling pre-built
artifacts) skip the slow path entirely. Keys + SSH config come from
the cid node’s `pangea-builder.nix` — no new auth plumbing.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use transports::`- [AtticTransport](https://docs.rs/transports/struct.AtticTransport.html);
- `pub use transports::`- [LocalTransport](https://docs.rs/transports/struct.LocalTransport.html);
- `pub use transports::`- [SshRemoteTransport](https://docs.rs/transports/struct.SshRemoteTransport.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [transports](https://docs.rs/transports/index.html)
- Concrete `BuildTransport`implementations.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Build](https://docs.rs/struct.BuildTransportChain.html)- Transport - Chain
- Declarative transport chain. A `None`field means “don’t try this transport”.
- [Layered](https://docs.rs/struct.LayeredTransport.html)- Transport
- Layered transport — tries each child in order, returns the first success.
- [Store](https://docs.rs/struct.StorePath.html)- Path
- A Nix store path — content-addressed handle.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Build](https://docs.rs/enum.BuildError.html)- Error
- [Build](https://docs.rs/enum.BuildRef.html)- Ref
- A reference to something that becomes a Nix store path.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [CRATE_](https://docs.rs/constant.CRATE_STATUS.html)- STATUS
- Phase marker. Bumped by each phase that lands a change.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Build](https://docs.rs/trait.BuildTransport.html)- Transport
- The operation-level transport trait. Phase H.5 implements
`AtticTransport`,`SshRemoteTransport`, and`LocalTransport`.

# fs_extra 1.3.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fs_extra/1.3.0

# fs_extra

A Rust library that provides additional functionality not present in [ std::fs](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/index.html).

## Key features:

-
Copy files (optionally with information about the progress).
-
Copy directories recursively (optionally with information about the progress).
-
Move files (optionally with information about the progress).
-
Move directories recursively (optionally with information about the progress).
-
A single method for create and write `String`content in file.
-
A single method for open and read `String`content from file.
-
Get folder size
-
Get collection of directory entries

## Functions:

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| [fs_extra::copy_items](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/fn.copy_items.html) | Recursively copies files and directories from one location to another |
| [fs_extra::copy_items_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/fn.copy_items_with_progress.html) | Recursively copies files and directories from one location to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::move_items](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/fn.move_items.html) | Recursively moves files and directories from one location to another |
| [fs_extra::move_items_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/fn.move_items_with_progress.html) | Recursively moves files and directories from one location to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::remove_items](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/fn.remove_items.html) | Removes files or directories |
| [fs_extra::file::copy](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.copy.html) | Copies the contents of one file to another |
| [fs_extra::file::copy_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.copy_with_progress.html) | Copies the contents of one file to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::file::move_file](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.move_file.html) | Moves a file from one location to another |
| [fs_extra::file::move_file_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.move_file_with_progress.html) | Moves a file from one location to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::file::remove](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.remove.html) | Removes a file |

| [fs_extra::file::write_all](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/file/fn.write_all.html) | Writes `String`content to a file |
| [fs_extra::dir::create](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.create.html) | Creates a new, empty directory at the given path |
| [fs_extra::dir::create_all](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.create_all.html) | Recursively creates a directory and all of its parent components if they are missing |
| [fs_extra::dir::copy](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.copy.html) | Recursively copies the directory contents from one location to another |
| [fs_extra::dir::copy_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.copy_with_progress.html) | Recursively copies the directory contents from one location to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::dir::move_dir](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.move_dir.html) | Moves directory contents from one location to another |
| [fs_extra::dir::move_dir_with_progress](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.move_dir_with_progress.html) | Moves directory contents from one location to another with information about progress |
| [fs_extra::dir::remove](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.remove.html) | Removes directory |
| [fs_extra::dir::get_size](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.get_size.html) | Returns the size of the file or directory |
| [fs_extra::dir::get_dir_content](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.get_dir_content.html) | Gets details such as the size and child items of a directory |
| [fs_extra::dir::get_dir_content2](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.get_dir_content2.html) | Gets details such as the size and child items of a directory using specified settings |
| [fs_extra::dir::get_details_entry](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.get_details_entry.html) | Gets attributes of a directory entry |
| [fs_extra::dir::ls](https://docs.rs/fs_extra/*/fs_extra/dir/fn.ls.html) | Gets attributes of directory entries in a directory |

## Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "1.3.0"
```
## Examples

The following example shows how to copy a directory recursively and display progress. First a source directory `./temp/dir` containing file `test1.txt` and a subdirectory `sub` is createad with `sub` itself having a file `test2.txt`. `./temp/dir` and all contents are then copied out to `./out/dir`.

```
use Path;
use ;
use ;
extern crate fs_extra;
use *;
use *;
```

# fs_extra - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fs_extra/1.3.0/target-redirect/fs_extra/

Copies a list of directories and files to another place recursively. This function will
also copy the permission bits of the original files to destination files (not for
directories).

Copies a list of directories and files to another place recursively, with
information about progress. This function will also copy the permission bits of the
original files to destination files (not for directories).

Moves a list of directories and files to another place recursively. This function will
also copy the permission bits of the original files to destination files (not for
directories).

Moves a list of directories and files to another place recursively, with
information about progress. This function will also copy the permission bits of the
original files to destination files (not for directories).

[156](https://docs.rs#156)use crate::error::*;
[157](https://docs.rs#157)use std::path::Path;
[158](https://docs.rs#158)
[159](https://docs.rs#159)/// Copies a list of directories and files to another place recursively. This function will
[160](https://docs.rs#160)/// also copy the permission bits of the original files to destination files (not for
[161](https://docs.rs#161)/// directories).
[162](https://docs.rs#162)///
[163](https://docs.rs#163)/// # Errors
[164](https://docs.rs#164)///
[165](https://docs.rs#165)/// This function will return an error in the following situations, but is not limited to just
[166](https://docs.rs#166)/// these case:
[167](https://docs.rs#167)///
[168](https://docs.rs#168)/// * List `from` contains  file or directory does not exist.
[169](https://docs.rs#169)///
[170](https://docs.rs#170)/// * List `from` contains  file or directory with invalid name.
[171](https://docs.rs#171)///
[172](https://docs.rs#172)/// * The current process does not have the permission to access to file from `lists from` or
[173](https://docs.rs#173)/// `to`.
[174](https://docs.rs#174)///
[175](https://docs.rs#175)/// # Example
[176](https://docs.rs#176)///
[177](https://docs.rs#177)/// ```rust,ignore
[178](https://docs.rs#178)///  extern crate fs_extra;
[179](https://docs.rs#179)///  use fs_extra::dir::copy;
[180](https://docs.rs#180)///
[181](https://docs.rs#181)///  let options = dir::CopyOptions::new(); //Initialize default values for CopyOptions
[182](https://docs.rs#182)///
[183](https://docs.rs#183)///  // copy dir1 and file1.txt to target/dir1 and target/file1.txt
[184](https://docs.rs#184)///  let mut from_paths = Vec::new();
[185](https://docs.rs#185)///  from_paths.push("source/dir1");
[186](https://docs.rs#186)///  from_paths.push("source/file.txt");
[187](https://docs.rs#187)///  copy_items(&from_paths, "target", &options)?;
[188](https://docs.rs#188)/// ```
[189](https://docs.rs#189)///
[190](https://docs.rs#190)pub fn copy_items<P, Q>(from: &[P], to: Q, options: &dir::CopyOptions) -> Result<u64>
[191](https://docs.rs#191)where
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    P: AsRef<Path>,
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    Q: AsRef<Path>,
[194](https://docs.rs#194){
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    let mut result: u64 = 0;
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    if options.content_only {
[197](https://docs.rs#197)        err!(
[198](https://docs.rs#198)            "Options 'content_only' not acccess for copy_items function",
[199](https://docs.rs#199)            ErrorKind::Other
[200](https://docs.rs#200)        );
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    }
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    for item in from {
[203](https://docs.rs#203)        let item = item.as_ref();
[204](https://docs.rs#204)        if item.is_dir() {
[205](https://docs.rs#205)            result += dir::copy(item, &to, options)?;
[206](https://docs.rs#206)        } else if let Some(file_name) = item.file_name() {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)            if let Some(file_name) = file_name.to_str() {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)                let file_options = file::CopyOptions {
[209](https://docs.rs#209)                    overwrite: options.overwrite,
[210](https://docs.rs#210)                    skip_exist: options.skip_exist,
[211](https://docs.rs#211)                    ..Default::default()
[212](https://docs.rs#212)                };
[213](https://docs.rs#213)                result += file::copy(item, to.as_ref().join(file_name), &file_options)?;
[214](https://docs.rs#214)            }
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        } else {
[216](https://docs.rs#216)            err!("Invalid file name", ErrorKind::InvalidFileName);
[217](https://docs.rs#217)        }
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    }
[219](https://docs.rs#219)
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    Ok(result)
[221](https://docs.rs#221)}
[222](https://docs.rs#222)
[223](https://docs.rs#223)/// A structure which includes information about the current status of copying or moving a directory.
[224](https://docs.rs#224)pub struct TransitProcess {
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    /// Already copied bytes
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    pub copied_bytes: u64,
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    /// All the bytes which should be copied or moved (dir size).
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    pub total_bytes: u64,
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    /// Copied bytes on this time for file.
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    pub file_bytes_copied: u64,
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    /// Size of currently copied file.
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    pub file_total_bytes: u64,
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    /// Name of currently copied file.
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    pub file_name: String,
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    /// Name of currently copied folder.
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    pub dir_name: String,
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    /// Transit state
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    pub state: dir::TransitState,
[239](https://docs.rs#239)}
[240](https://docs.rs#240)
[241](https://docs.rs#241)impl Clone for TransitProcess {

[245](https://docs.rs#245)            total_bytes: self.total_bytes,
[246](https://docs.rs#246)            file_bytes_copied: self.file_bytes_copied,

[248](https://docs.rs#248)            file_name: self.file_name.clone(),
[249](https://docs.rs#249)            dir_name: self.dir_name.clone(),

[254](https://docs.rs#254)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)/// Copies a list of directories and files to another place recursively, with
[256](https://docs.rs#256)/// information about progress. This function will also copy the permission bits of the
[257](https://docs.rs#257)/// original files to destination files (not for directories).
[258](https://docs.rs#258)///
[259](https://docs.rs#259)/// # Errors
[260](https://docs.rs#260)///
[261](https://docs.rs#261)/// This function will return an error in the following situations, but is not limited to just
[262](https://docs.rs#262)/// these case:
[263](https://docs.rs#263)///
[264](https://docs.rs#264)/// * List `from` contains  file or directory does not exist.
[265](https://docs.rs#265)///
[266](https://docs.rs#266)/// * List `from` contains  file or directory with invalid name.
[267](https://docs.rs#267)///
[268](https://docs.rs#268)/// * The current process does not have the permission to access to file from `lists from` or
[269](https://docs.rs#269)/// `to`.
[270](https://docs.rs#270)///
[271](https://docs.rs#271)/// # Example
[272](https://docs.rs#272)/// ```rust,ignore
[273](https://docs.rs#273)///
[274](https://docs.rs#274)///  extern crate fs_extra;
[275](https://docs.rs#275)///  use fs_extra::dir::copy;
[276](https://docs.rs#276)///
[277](https://docs.rs#277)///  let options = dir::CopyOptions::new(); //Initialize default values for CopyOptions
[278](https://docs.rs#278)///  let handle = |process_info: TransitProcess| {
[279](https://docs.rs#279)///     println!("{}", process_info.total_bytes);
[280](https://docs.rs#280)///     fs_extra::dir::TransitProcessResult::ContinueOrAbort
[281](https://docs.rs#281)///  }
[282](https://docs.rs#282)///  // copy dir1 and file1.txt to target/dir1 and target/file1.txt
[283](https://docs.rs#283)///  let mut from_paths = Vec::new();
[284](https://docs.rs#284)///  from_paths.push("source/dir1");
[285](https://docs.rs#285)///  from_paths.push("source/file.txt");
[286](https://docs.rs#286)///  copy_items_with_progress(&from_paths, "target", &options, handle)?;
[287](https://docs.rs#287)/// ```
[288](https://docs.rs#288)///
[289](https://docs.rs#289)pub fn copy_items_with_progress<P, Q, F>(
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    from: &[P],
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    to: Q,
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    options: &dir::CopyOptions,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    mut progress_handler: F,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)) -> Result<u64>
[295](https://docs.rs#295)where
[296](https://docs.rs#296)    P: AsRef<Path>,
[297](https://docs.rs#297)    Q: AsRef<Path>,
[298](https://docs.rs#298)    F: FnMut(TransitProcess) -> dir::TransitProcessResult,
[299](https://docs.rs#299){
[300](https://docs.rs#300)    if options.content_only {
[301](https://docs.rs#301)        err!(
[302](https://docs.rs#302)            "Options 'content_only' not access for copy_items_with_progress function",
[303](https://docs.rs#303)            ErrorKind::Other
[304](https://docs.rs#304)        );
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    }
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    let mut total_size = 0;
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    let mut list_paths = Vec::new();
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    for item in from {
[309](https://docs.rs#309)        let item = item.as_ref();
[310](https://docs.rs#310)        total_size += dir::get_size(item)?;
[311](https://docs.rs#311)        list_paths.push(item);
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    }
[313](https://docs.rs#313)
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    let mut result: u64 = 0;
[315](https://docs.rs#315)    let mut info_process = TransitProcess {
[316](https://docs.rs#316)        copied_bytes: 0,
[317](https://docs.rs#317)        total_bytes: total_size,
[318](https://docs.rs#318)        file_bytes_copied: 0,
[319](https://docs.rs#319)        file_total_bytes: 0,
[320](https://docs.rs#320)        file_name: String::new(),
[321](https://docs.rs#321)        dir_name: String::new(),
[322](https://docs.rs#322)        state: dir::TransitState::Normal,
[323](https://docs.rs#323)    };
[324](https://docs.rs#324)
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    let mut options = options.clone();
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    for item in list_paths {
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        if item.is_dir() {
[328](https://docs.rs#328)            if let Some(dir_name) = item.components().last() {
[329](https://docs.rs#329)                if let Ok(dir_name) = dir_name.as_os_str().to_os_string().into_string() {
[330](https://docs.rs#330)                    info_process.dir_name = dir_name;
[331](https://docs.rs#331)                } else {
[332](https://docs.rs#332)                    err!("Invalid folder from", ErrorKind::InvalidFolder);
[333](https://docs.rs#333)                }
[334](https://docs.rs#334)            } else {
[335](https://docs.rs#335)                err!("Invalid folder from", ErrorKind::InvalidFolder);
[336](https://docs.rs#336)            }
[337](https://docs.rs#337)
[338](https://docs.rs#338)            let copied_bytes = result;
[339](https://docs.rs#339)            let dir_options = options.clone();
[340](https://docs.rs#340)            let handler = |info: dir::TransitProcess| {
[341](https://docs.rs#341)                info_process.copied_bytes = copied_bytes + info.copied_bytes;
[342](https://docs.rs#342)                info_process.state = info.state;
[343](https://docs.rs#343)                let result = progress_handler(info_process.clone());
[344](https://docs.rs#344)                match result {
[345](https://docs.rs#345)                    dir::TransitProcessResult::OverwriteAll => options.overwrite = true,
[346](https://docs.rs#346)                    dir::TransitProcessResult::SkipAll => options.skip_exist = true,
[347](https://docs.rs#347)                    _ => {}
[348](https://docs.rs#348)                }
[349](https://docs.rs#349)                result
[350](https://docs.rs#350)            };
[351](https://docs.rs#351)            result += dir::copy_with_progress(item, &to, &dir_options, handler)?;
[352](https://docs.rs#352)        } else {
[353](https://docs.rs#353)            let mut file_options = file::CopyOptions {
[354](https://docs.rs#354)                overwrite: options.overwrite,
[355](https://docs.rs#355)                skip_exist: options.skip_exist,
[356](https://docs.rs#356)                buffer_size: options.buffer_size,
[357](https://docs.rs#357)            };
[358](https://docs.rs#358)
[359](https://docs.rs#359)            if let Some(file_name) = item.file_name() {
[360](https://docs.rs#360)                if let Some(file_name) = file_name.to_str() {
[361](https://docs.rs#361)                    info_process.file_name = file_name.to_string();
[362](https://docs.rs#362)                } else {
[363](https://docs.rs#363)                    err!("Invalid file name", ErrorKind::InvalidFileName);
[364](https://docs.rs#364)                }
[365](https://docs.rs#365)            } else {
[366](https://docs.rs#366)                err!("Invalid file name", ErrorKind::InvalidFileName);
[367](https://docs.rs#367)            }
[368](https://docs.rs#368)
[369](https://docs.rs#369)            info_process.file_bytes_copied = 0;
[370](https://docs.rs#370)            info_process.file_total_bytes = item.metadata()?.len();
[371](https://docs.rs#371)
[372](https://docs.rs#372)            let copied_bytes = result;
[373](https://docs.rs#373)            let file_name = to.as_ref().join(info_process.file_name.clone());
[374](https://docs.rs#374)            let mut work = true;
[375](https://docs.rs#375)
[376](https://docs.rs#376)            let mut result_copy: Result<u64>;
[377](https://docs.rs#377)            while work {
[378](https://docs.rs#378)                {
[379](https://docs.rs#379)                    let handler = |info: file::TransitProcess| {
[380](https://docs.rs#380)                        info_process.copied_bytes = copied_bytes + info.copied_bytes;
[381](https://docs.rs#381)                        info_process.file_bytes_copied = info.copied_bytes;
[382](https://docs.rs#382)                        progress_handler(info_process.clone());
[383](https://docs.rs#383)                    };
[384](https://docs.rs#384)                    result_copy =
[385](https://docs.rs#385)                        file::copy_with_progress(item, &file_name, &file_options, handler);
[386](https://docs.rs#386)                }
[387](https://docs.rs#387)                match result_copy {
[388](https://docs.rs#388)                    Ok(val) => {
[389](https://docs.rs#389)                        result += val;
[390](https://docs.rs#390)                        work = false;
[391](https://docs.rs#391)                    }
[392](https://docs.rs#392)                    Err(err) => match err.kind {
[393](https://docs.rs#393)                        ErrorKind::AlreadyExists => {
[394](https://docs.rs#394)                            let mut info_process = info_process.clone();
[395](https://docs.rs#395)                            info_process.state = dir::TransitState::Exists;
[396](https://docs.rs#396)                            let user_decide = progress_handler(info_process);
[397](https://docs.rs#397)                            match user_decide {
[398](https://docs.rs#398)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Overwrite => {
[399](https://docs.rs#399)                                    file_options.overwrite = true;
[400](https://docs.rs#400)                                }
[401](https://docs.rs#401)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::OverwriteAll => {
[402](https://docs.rs#402)                                    file_options.overwrite = true;
[403](https://docs.rs#403)                                    options.overwrite = true;
[404](https://docs.rs#404)                                }
[405](https://docs.rs#405)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Skip => {
[406](https://docs.rs#406)                                    file_options.skip_exist = true;
[407](https://docs.rs#407)                                }
[408](https://docs.rs#408)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::SkipAll => {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)                                    file_options.skip_exist = true;
[410](https://docs.rs#410)                                    options.skip_exist = true;
[411](https://docs.rs#411)                                }
[412](https://docs.rs#412)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Retry => {}
[413](https://docs.rs#413)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::ContinueOrAbort => {
[414](https://docs.rs#414)                                    let err_msg = err.to_string();
[415](https://docs.rs#415)                                    err!(err_msg.as_str(), err.kind)
[416](https://docs.rs#416)                                }
[417](https://docs.rs#417)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Abort => {
[418](https://docs.rs#418)                                    let err_msg = err.to_string();
[419](https://docs.rs#419)                                    err!(err_msg.as_str(), err.kind)
[420](https://docs.rs#420)                                }
[421](https://docs.rs#421)                            }
[422](https://docs.rs#422)                        }
[423](https://docs.rs#423)                        ErrorKind::PermissionDenied => {
[424](https://docs.rs#424)                            let mut info_process = info_process.clone();
[425](https://docs.rs#425)                            info_process.state = dir::TransitState::Exists;
[426](https://docs.rs#426)                            let user_decide = progress_handler(info_process);
[427](https://docs.rs#427)                            match user_decide {
[428](https://docs.rs#428)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Overwrite => {
[429](https://docs.rs#429)                                    err!("Overwrite denied for this situation!", ErrorKind::Other);
[430](https://docs.rs#430)                                }
[431](https://docs.rs#431)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::OverwriteAll => {
[432](https://docs.rs#432)                                    err!("Overwrite denied for this situation!", ErrorKind::Other);
[433](https://docs.rs#433)                                }
[434](https://docs.rs#434)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Skip => {
[435](https://docs.rs#435)                                    file_options.skip_exist = true;
[436](https://docs.rs#436)                                }
[437](https://docs.rs#437)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::SkipAll => {
[438](https://docs.rs#438)                                    file_options.skip_exist = true;
[439](https://docs.rs#439)                                    options.skip_exist = true;
[440](https://docs.rs#440)                                }
[441](https://docs.rs#441)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Retry => {}
[442](https://docs.rs#442)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::ContinueOrAbort => {
[443](https://docs.rs#443)                                    let err_msg = err.to_string();
[444](https://docs.rs#444)                                    err!(err_msg.as_str(), err.kind)
[445](https://docs.rs#445)                                }
[446](https://docs.rs#446)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Abort => {
[447](https://docs.rs#447)                                    let err_msg = err.to_string();
[448](https://docs.rs#448)                                    err!(err_msg.as_str(), err.kind)
[449](https://docs.rs#449)                                }
[450](https://docs.rs#450)                            }
[451](https://docs.rs#451)                        }
[452](https://docs.rs#452)                        _ => {
[453](https://docs.rs#453)                            let err_msg = err.to_string();
[454](https://docs.rs#454)                            err!(err_msg.as_str(), err.kind)
[455](https://docs.rs#455)                        }
[456](https://docs.rs#456)                    },
[457](https://docs.rs#457)                }
[458](https://docs.rs#458)            }
[459](https://docs.rs#459)        }
[460](https://docs.rs#460)    }
[461](https://docs.rs#461)
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    Ok(result)
[463](https://docs.rs#463)}
[464](https://docs.rs#464)
[465](https://docs.rs#465)/// Moves a list of directories and files to another place recursively. This function will
[466](https://docs.rs#466)/// also copy the permission bits of the original files to destination files (not for
[467](https://docs.rs#467)/// directories).
[468](https://docs.rs#468)///
[469](https://docs.rs#469)/// # Errors
[470](https://docs.rs#470)///
[471](https://docs.rs#471)/// This function will return an error in the following situations, but is not limited to just
[472](https://docs.rs#472)/// these case:
[473](https://docs.rs#473)///
[474](https://docs.rs#474)/// * List `from` contains  file or directory does not exist.
[475](https://docs.rs#475)///
[476](https://docs.rs#476)/// * List `from` contains  file or directory with invalid name.
[477](https://docs.rs#477)///
[478](https://docs.rs#478)/// * The current process does not have the permission to access to file from `lists from` or
[479](https://docs.rs#479)/// `to`.
[480](https://docs.rs#480)///
[481](https://docs.rs#481)/// # Example
[482](https://docs.rs#482)///
[483](https://docs.rs#483)/// ```rust,ignore
[484](https://docs.rs#484)///  extern crate fs_extra;
[485](https://docs.rs#485)///  use fs_extra::dir::copy;
[486](https://docs.rs#486)///
[487](https://docs.rs#487)///  let options = dir::CopyOptions::new(); //Initialize default values for CopyOptions
[488](https://docs.rs#488)///
[489](https://docs.rs#489)///  // move dir1 and file1.txt to target/dir1 and target/file1.txt
[490](https://docs.rs#490)///  let mut from_paths = Vec::new();
[491](https://docs.rs#491)///  from_paths.push("source/dir1");
[492](https://docs.rs#492)///  from_paths.push("source/file.txt");
[493](https://docs.rs#493)///  move_items(&from_paths, "target", &options)?;
[494](https://docs.rs#494)/// ```
[495](https://docs.rs#495)///
[496](https://docs.rs#496)pub fn move_items<P, Q>(from_items: &[P], to: Q, options: &dir::CopyOptions) -> Result<u64>
[497](https://docs.rs#497)where
[498](https://docs.rs#498)    P: AsRef<Path>,
[499](https://docs.rs#499)    Q: AsRef<Path>,
[500](https://docs.rs#500){
[501](https://docs.rs#501)    if options.content_only {
[502](https://docs.rs#502)        err!(
[503](https://docs.rs#503)            "Options 'content_only' not access for move_items function",
[504](https://docs.rs#504)            ErrorKind::Other
[505](https://docs.rs#505)        );
[506](https://docs.rs#506)    }
[507](https://docs.rs#507)    let mut total_size = 0;
[508](https://docs.rs#508)    let mut list_paths = Vec::new();
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    for item in from_items {
[510](https://docs.rs#510)        let item = item.as_ref();
[511](https://docs.rs#511)        total_size += dir::get_size(item)?;
[512](https://docs.rs#512)        list_paths.push(item);
[513](https://docs.rs#513)    }
[514](https://docs.rs#514)
[515](https://docs.rs#515)    let mut result = 0;
[516](https://docs.rs#516)    let mut info_process = TransitProcess {
[517](https://docs.rs#517)        copied_bytes: 0,
[518](https://docs.rs#518)        total_bytes: total_size,
[519](https://docs.rs#519)        file_bytes_copied: 0,
[520](https://docs.rs#520)        file_total_bytes: 0,
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        file_name: String::new(),
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        dir_name: String::new(),
[523](https://docs.rs#523)        state: dir::TransitState::Normal,
[524](https://docs.rs#524)    };
[525](https://docs.rs#525)
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    for item in list_paths {
[527](https://docs.rs#527)        if item.is_dir() {
[528](https://docs.rs#528)            if let Some(dir_name) = item.components().last() {
[529](https://docs.rs#529)                if let Ok(dir_name) = dir_name.as_os_str().to_os_string().into_string() {
[530](https://docs.rs#530)                    info_process.dir_name = dir_name;
[531](https://docs.rs#531)                } else {
[532](https://docs.rs#532)                    err!("Invalid folder from", ErrorKind::InvalidFolder);
[533](https://docs.rs#533)                }
[534](https://docs.rs#534)            } else {
[535](https://docs.rs#535)                err!("Invalid folder from", ErrorKind::InvalidFolder);
[536](https://docs.rs#536)            }
[537](https://docs.rs#537)
[538](https://docs.rs#538)            result += dir::move_dir(item, &to, options)?;
[539](https://docs.rs#539)        } else {
[540](https://docs.rs#540)            let file_options = file::CopyOptions {
[541](https://docs.rs#541)                overwrite: options.overwrite,
[542](https://docs.rs#542)                skip_exist: options.skip_exist,
[543](https://docs.rs#543)                buffer_size: options.buffer_size,
[544](https://docs.rs#544)            };
[545](https://docs.rs#545)
[546](https://docs.rs#546)            if let Some(file_name) = item.file_name() {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)                if let Some(file_name) = file_name.to_str() {
[548](https://docs.rs#548)                    info_process.file_name = file_name.to_string();
[549](https://docs.rs#549)                } else {
[550](https://docs.rs#550)                    err!("Invalid file name", ErrorKind::InvalidFileName);
[551](https://docs.rs#551)                }
[552](https://docs.rs#552)            } else {
[553](https://docs.rs#553)                err!("Invalid file name", ErrorKind::InvalidFileName);
[554](https://docs.rs#554)            }
[555](https://docs.rs#555)
[556](https://docs.rs#556)            info_process.file_bytes_copied = 0;
[557](https://docs.rs#557)            info_process.file_total_bytes = item.metadata()?.len();
[558](https://docs.rs#558)
[559](https://docs.rs#559)            let file_name = to.as_ref().join(info_process.file_name.clone());
[560](https://docs.rs#560)            result += file::move_file(item, &file_name, &file_options)?;
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        }
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    }
[563](https://docs.rs#563)
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    Ok(result)
[565](https://docs.rs#565)}
[566](https://docs.rs#566)
[567](https://docs.rs#567)/// Moves a list of directories and files to another place recursively, with
[568](https://docs.rs#568)/// information about progress. This function will also copy the permission bits of the
[569](https://docs.rs#569)/// original files to destination files (not for directories).
[570](https://docs.rs#570)///
[571](https://docs.rs#571)/// # Errors
[572](https://docs.rs#572)///
[573](https://docs.rs#573)/// This function will return an error in the following situations, but is not limited to just
[574](https://docs.rs#574)/// these case:
[575](https://docs.rs#575)///
[576](https://docs.rs#576)/// * List `from` contains  file or directory does not exist.
[577](https://docs.rs#577)///
[578](https://docs.rs#578)/// * List `from` contains  file or directory with invalid name.
[579](https://docs.rs#579)///
[580](https://docs.rs#580)/// * The current process does not have the permission to access to file from `lists from` or
[581](https://docs.rs#581)/// `to`.
[582](https://docs.rs#582)///
[583](https://docs.rs#583)/// # Example
[584](https://docs.rs#584)///
[585](https://docs.rs#585)/// ```rust,ignore
[586](https://docs.rs#586)///  extern crate fs_extra;
[587](https://docs.rs#587)///  use fs_extra::dir::copy;
[588](https://docs.rs#588)///
[589](https://docs.rs#589)///  let options = dir::CopyOptions::new(); //Initialize default values for CopyOptions
[590](https://docs.rs#590)///  let handle = |process_info: TransitProcess| {
[591](https://docs.rs#591)///     println!("{}", process_info.total_bytes);
[592](https://docs.rs#592)///     fs_extra::dir::TransitProcessResult::ContinueOrAbort
[593](https://docs.rs#593)///  }
[594](https://docs.rs#594)///  // move dir1 and file1.txt to target/dir1 and target/file1.txt
[595](https://docs.rs#595)///  let mut from_paths = Vec::new();
[596](https://docs.rs#596)///  from_paths.push("source/dir1");
[597](https://docs.rs#597)///  from_paths.push("source/file.txt");
[598](https://docs.rs#598)///  move_items_with_progress(&from_paths, "target", &options, handle)?;
[599](https://docs.rs#599)/// ```
[600](https://docs.rs#600)///
[601](https://docs.rs#601)pub fn move_items_with_progress<P, Q, F>(
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    from_items: &[P],
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    to: Q,
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    options: &dir::CopyOptions,
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    mut progress_handler: F,
[606](https://docs.rs#606)) -> Result<u64>
[607](https://docs.rs#607)where
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    P: AsRef<Path>,
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    Q: AsRef<Path>,
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    F: FnMut(TransitProcess) -> dir::TransitProcessResult,
[611](https://docs.rs#611){
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    if options.content_only {
[613](https://docs.rs#613)        err!(
[614](https://docs.rs#614)            "Options 'content_only' not access for move_items_with_progress function",
[615](https://docs.rs#615)            ErrorKind::Other
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        );
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    }
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    let mut total_size = 0;
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    let mut list_paths = Vec::new();
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    for item in from_items {
[621](https://docs.rs#621)        let item = item.as_ref();
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        total_size += dir::get_size(item)?;
[623](https://docs.rs#623)        list_paths.push(item);
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    }
[625](https://docs.rs#625)
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    let mut result = 0;
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    let mut info_process = TransitProcess {
[628](https://docs.rs#628)        copied_bytes: 0,
[629](https://docs.rs#629)        total_bytes: total_size,
[630](https://docs.rs#630)        file_bytes_copied: 0,
[631](https://docs.rs#631)        file_total_bytes: 0,
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        file_name: String::new(),
[633](https://docs.rs#633)        dir_name: String::new(),
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        state: dir::TransitState::Normal,
[635](https://docs.rs#635)    };
[636](https://docs.rs#636)    let mut options = options.clone();
[637](https://docs.rs#637)
[638](https://docs.rs#638)    for item in list_paths {
[639](https://docs.rs#639)        if item.is_dir() {
[640](https://docs.rs#640)            if let Some(dir_name) = item.components().last() {
[641](https://docs.rs#641)                if let Ok(dir_name) = dir_name.as_os_str().to_os_string().into_string() {
[642](https://docs.rs#642)                    info_process.dir_name = dir_name;
[643](https://docs.rs#643)                } else {
[644](https://docs.rs#644)                    err!("Invalid folder from", ErrorKind::InvalidFolder);
[645](https://docs.rs#645)                }
[646](https://docs.rs#646)            } else {
[647](https://docs.rs#647)                err!("Invalid folder from", ErrorKind::InvalidFolder);
[648](https://docs.rs#648)            }
[649](https://docs.rs#649)
[650](https://docs.rs#650)            let copied_bytes = result;
[651](https://docs.rs#651)            let dir_options = options.clone();
[652](https://docs.rs#652)            let handler = |info: dir::TransitProcess| {
[653](https://docs.rs#653)                info_process.copied_bytes = copied_bytes + info.copied_bytes;
[654](https://docs.rs#654)                info_process.state = info.state;
[655](https://docs.rs#655)                let result = progress_handler(info_process.clone());
[656](https://docs.rs#656)                match result {
[657](https://docs.rs#657)                    dir::TransitProcessResult::OverwriteAll => options.overwrite = true,
[658](https://docs.rs#658)                    dir::TransitProcessResult::SkipAll => options.skip_exist = true,
[659](https://docs.rs#659)                    _ => {}
[660](https://docs.rs#660)                }
[661](https://docs.rs#661)                result
[662](https://docs.rs#662)            };
[663](https://docs.rs#663)            result += dir::move_dir_with_progress(item, &to, &dir_options, handler)?;
[664](https://docs.rs#664)        } else {
[665](https://docs.rs#665)            let mut file_options = file::CopyOptions {
[666](https://docs.rs#666)                overwrite: options.overwrite,
[667](https://docs.rs#667)                skip_exist: options.skip_exist,
[668](https://docs.rs#668)                buffer_size: options.buffer_size,
[669](https://docs.rs#669)            };
[670](https://docs.rs#670)
[671](https://docs.rs#671)            if let Some(file_name) = item.file_name() {
[672](https://docs.rs#672)                if let Some(file_name) = file_name.to_str() {
[673](https://docs.rs#673)                    info_process.file_name = file_name.to_string();
[674](https://docs.rs#674)                } else {
[675](https://docs.rs#675)                    err!("Invalid file name", ErrorKind::InvalidFileName);
[676](https://docs.rs#676)                }
[677](https://docs.rs#677)            } else {
[678](https://docs.rs#678)                err!("Invalid file name", ErrorKind::InvalidFileName);
[679](https://docs.rs#679)            }
[680](https://docs.rs#680)
[681](https://docs.rs#681)            info_process.file_bytes_copied = 0;
[682](https://docs.rs#682)            info_process.file_total_bytes = item.metadata()?.len();
[683](https://docs.rs#683)
[684](https://docs.rs#684)            let copied_bytes = result;
[685](https://docs.rs#685)            let file_name = to.as_ref().join(info_process.file_name.clone());
[686](https://docs.rs#686)            let mut work = true;
[687](https://docs.rs#687)
[688](https://docs.rs#688)            let mut result_copy: Result<u64>;
[689](https://docs.rs#689)            while work {
[690](https://docs.rs#690)                {
[691](https://docs.rs#691)                    let handler = |info: file::TransitProcess| {
[692](https://docs.rs#692)                        info_process.copied_bytes = copied_bytes + info.copied_bytes;
[693](https://docs.rs#693)                        info_process.file_bytes_copied = info.copied_bytes;
[694](https://docs.rs#694)                        progress_handler(info_process.clone());
[695](https://docs.rs#695)                    };
[696](https://docs.rs#696)                    result_copy =
[697](https://docs.rs#697)                        file::move_file_with_progress(item, &file_name, &file_options, handler);
[698](https://docs.rs#698)                }
[699](https://docs.rs#699)                match result_copy {
[700](https://docs.rs#700)                    Ok(val) => {
[701](https://docs.rs#701)                        result += val;
[702](https://docs.rs#702)                        work = false;
[703](https://docs.rs#703)                    }
[704](https://docs.rs#704)                    Err(err) => match err.kind {
[705](https://docs.rs#705)                        ErrorKind::AlreadyExists => {
[706](https://docs.rs#706)                            let mut info_process = info_process.clone();
[707](https://docs.rs#707)                            info_process.state = dir::TransitState::Exists;
[708](https://docs.rs#708)                            let user_decide = progress_handler(info_process);
[709](https://docs.rs#709)                            match user_decide {
[710](https://docs.rs#710)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Overwrite => {
[711](https://docs.rs#711)                                    file_options.overwrite = true;
[712](https://docs.rs#712)                                }
[713](https://docs.rs#713)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::OverwriteAll => {
[714](https://docs.rs#714)                                    file_options.overwrite = true;
[715](https://docs.rs#715)                                    options.overwrite = true;
[716](https://docs.rs#716)                                }
[717](https://docs.rs#717)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Skip => {
[718](https://docs.rs#718)                                    file_options.skip_exist = true;
[719](https://docs.rs#719)                                }
[720](https://docs.rs#720)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::SkipAll => {
[721](https://docs.rs#721)                                    file_options.skip_exist = true;
[722](https://docs.rs#722)                                    options.skip_exist = true;
[723](https://docs.rs#723)                                }
[724](https://docs.rs#724)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Retry => {}
[725](https://docs.rs#725)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::ContinueOrAbort => {
[726](https://docs.rs#726)                                    let err_msg = err.to_string();
[727](https://docs.rs#727)                                    err!(err_msg.as_str(), err.kind)
[728](https://docs.rs#728)                                }
[729](https://docs.rs#729)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Abort => {
[730](https://docs.rs#730)                                    let err_msg = err.to_string();
[731](https://docs.rs#731)                                    err!(err_msg.as_str(), err.kind)
[732](https://docs.rs#732)                                }
[733](https://docs.rs#733)                            }
[734](https://docs.rs#734)                        }
[735](https://docs.rs#735)                        ErrorKind::PermissionDenied => {
[736](https://docs.rs#736)                            let mut info_process = info_process.clone();
[737](https://docs.rs#737)                            info_process.state = dir::TransitState::Exists;
[738](https://docs.rs#738)                            let user_decide = progress_handler(info_process);
[739](https://docs.rs#739)                            match user_decide {
[740](https://docs.rs#740)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Overwrite => {
[741](https://docs.rs#741)                                    err!("Overwrite denied for this situation!", ErrorKind::Other);
[742](https://docs.rs#742)                                }
[743](https://docs.rs#743)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::OverwriteAll => {
[744](https://docs.rs#744)                                    err!("Overwrite denied for this situation!", ErrorKind::Other);
[745](https://docs.rs#745)                                }
[746](https://docs.rs#746)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Skip => {
[747](https://docs.rs#747)                                    file_options.skip_exist = true;
[748](https://docs.rs#748)                                }
[749](https://docs.rs#749)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::SkipAll => {
[750](https://docs.rs#750)                                    file_options.skip_exist = true;
[751](https://docs.rs#751)                                    options.skip_exist = true;
[752](https://docs.rs#752)                                }
[753](https://docs.rs#753)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Retry => {}
[754](https://docs.rs#754)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::ContinueOrAbort => {
[755](https://docs.rs#755)                                    let err_msg = err.to_string();
[756](https://docs.rs#756)                                    err!(err_msg.as_str(), err.kind)
[757](https://docs.rs#757)                                }
[758](https://docs.rs#758)                                dir::TransitProcessResult::Abort => {
[759](https://docs.rs#759)                                    let err_msg = err.to_string();
[760](https://docs.rs#760)                                    err!(err_msg.as_str(), err.kind)
[761](https://docs.rs#761)                                }
[762](https://docs.rs#762)                            }
[763](https://docs.rs#763)                        }
[764](https://docs.rs#764)                        _ => {

[766](https://docs.rs#766)                            err!(err_msg.as_str(), err.kind)
[767](https://docs.rs#767)                        }
[768](https://docs.rs#768)                    },

# fs_extra::dir - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fs_extra/1.3.0/fs_extra/dir/index.html

## Expand description

This module includes additional methods for working with directories.

One of the additional features is information about process and recursion operations.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use std::path::Path;
use std::{thread, time};
use std::sync::mpsc::{self, TryRecvError};
extern crate fs_extra;
use fs_extra::dir::*;
use fs_extra::error::*;
fn example_copy() -> Result<()> {
    let path_from = Path::new("./temp");
    let path_to = path_from.join("out");
    let test_folder = path_from.join("test_folder");
    let dir = test_folder.join("dir");
    let sub = dir.join("sub");
    let file1 = dir.join("file1.txt");
    let file2 = sub.join("file2.txt");
    create_all(&sub, true)?;
    create_all(&path_to, true)?;
    fs_extra::file::write_all(&file1, "content1")?;
    fs_extra::file::write_all(&file2, "content2")?;
    assert!(dir.exists());
    assert!(sub.exists());
    assert!(file1.exists());
    assert!(file2.exists());
    let options = CopyOptions {
        buffer_size: 1,
        ..Default::default(),
    };
    let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
    thread::spawn(move || {
        let handler = |process_info: TransitProcess| {
            tx.send(process_info).unwrap();
            thread::sleep(time::Duration::from_millis(500));
        };
        copy_with_progress(&test_folder, &path_to, &options, handler).unwrap();
    });
    loop {
        match rx.try_recv() {
            Ok(process_info) => {
                println!("{} of {} bytes",
                         process_info.copied_bytes,
                         process_info.total_bytes);
            }
            Err(TryRecvError::Disconnected) => {
                println!("finished");
                break;
            }
            Err(TryRecvError::Empty) => {}
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
fn main() {
    example_copy();
}
```

- Copies the directory contents from one place to another using recursive method. This function will also copy the permission bits of the original files to destination files (not for directories).
- [copy_](https://docs.rs/fn.copy_with_progress.html)- with_ - progress
- Copies the directory contents from one place to another using recursive method, with information about progress. This function will also copy the permission bits of the original files to destination files (not for directories).

- Creates a new, empty directory at the provided path.

- Return DirContent which contains information about directory:
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_dir_content2.html)- dir_ - content2
- Return DirContent which contains information about directory:
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_size.html)- size
- Returns the size of the file or directory in bytes.(!important: folders size not count)
- [ls](https://docs.rs/fn.ls.html)
- Returns a collection of directory entries with attributes specifying the information that should be returned.
- [move_](https://docs.rs/fn.move_dir.html)- dir
- Moves the directory contents from one place to another. This function will also copy the permission bits of the original files to destination files (not for directories).
- [move_](https://docs.rs/fn.move_dir_with_progress.html)- dir_ - with_ - progress
- Moves the directory contents from one place to another with information about progress. This function will also copy the permission bits of the original files to destination files (not for directories).
- [remove](https://docs.rs/fn.remove.html)
- Removes directory.
